title: Spritesheets Schema
description: Schema for spritesheets using enum names as keys

sprites.description: Map of sprite enum names to their metadata

spriteMetadata.description: Metadata for a single sprite type

zorder.description:
Render order (draw lowest first). By default an entity's zorder is its y-position, so sprites lower on screen draw in front. A value of 0 means 'no explicit zorder': use that default.

Indexing:
- Obstacles and walls: one entry per sprite variant (indexed by the sprite index / frame_index_offset).
- Multiblocks: one entry per grid cell, row-major (index = row * grid_size.x + col). Each segment gets y + zorder[cell]; the root uses the entry for its sprite index.
- Everything else (NPCs, runes, gates, chests, etc.) only reads zorder[0].
- An index past the end of the list falls back to 0 (debug log only). So [0] is a valid 'use defaults everywhere'.

How a value is applied depends on who creates the entity:
- Obstacles (decorate_obstacle): an explicit zorder passed by code wins, then a non-zero json value, then the y-position. A non-zero json value is ABSOLUTE (it replaces y). Crypt and passage obstacles instead pass y + zorder[idx], making the value RELATIVE.
- Walls: a non-zero value is ABSOLUTE, otherwise y + sprite height.
- Multiblock roots: an explicit code value wins, then y + a non-zero json value (RELATIVE), then y.
- Multiblock segments and NPCs: always y + value (RELATIVE).
- Rune markers, ruin stairs gate, shadow hand: ABSOLUTE zorder[0].

Relative values are small offsets around y (e.g. -5, 2, 64). Absolute values are large (e.g. 10000, 100000) to always draw above or below the y-sorted world. Any non-zero entry makes the sheet count as having an explicit zorder (SpriteSheet::has_zorder), which flight honours: a flying player stays behind it where their ground ordering would.

indices_per_sequence.description: How many 'sprite_indices' entries the animation loops over, one per animation frame. 1 = static sprite.

framerate.description: Animation framerate in frames per second. 0 = not animated. Use 0 for single-frame sprites.

grid_size.description: width and height grid size for the multi-sprite

walking_collision_mask.description: Which cells of the sprite collide, one boolean per 'grid_size' cell in row-major order (left to right, top to bottom). For NPCs these are the cells it stands on, used for collision and pathfinding clearance. Shortcut: a single entry (e.g. [true]) applies that value to every cell, whatever the 'grid_size'. Otherwise there must be at least one entry per cell. If omitted, every cell collides. All false is valid: the sprite does not collide (an NPC then logs a warning at spawn and cannot touch the player).

flying_collision_mask.description: Which cells block the player while flying on the witchesbroom. Same format as walking_collision_mask: one boolean per grid_size cell in row-major order, or a single entry applied to every cell. If omitted, flight blocking falls back to the size-based rule (walls and multiblocks larger than 1x1 block, other sprites can be flown over).

sprite_indices.description: Array of sprite indices in the texture
